sentenceSets.sentence: The forecast struck the board as pollyannaish, since it assumed record sales in each of the next five quarters and no competitor response at all.

answerChoices.reasoning: The sentence does not merely say the forecast leaned hopeful; it shows the projection ignoring competitors entirely, which marks a refusal to see anything unfavorable rather than a cheerful reading of real odds.
An ambitious forecast would set a hard target and acknowledge what stands in the way, but this one erases the obstacle by assuming no competitor reacts.
Speculative projections admit their own uncertainty, whereas the board's objection is that this one treats an unbroken run of records as settled.
An aggressive plan pushes hard against known resistance, and the flaw here is that the plan does not register resistance in the first place.
A provisional figure is offered subject to revision, which would not have troubled the board the way an unqualified five-quarter run of records did.
Meticulous work would have accounted for competitor response rather than omitting it.
The complaint concerns assumptions about the future, not that the forecast was built on outdated information.
Confidentiality concerns who may see the forecast and has nothing to do with the board's objection to its assumptions.
A forecast assuming record sales every quarter is the opposite of gloomy.
The board faults the assumptions as unrealistically rosy, not as deliberately falsified.
A physical condition of saturation cannot describe a sales forecast.

sentenceSets.sentence: After the third flood, the mayor's pollyannaish insistence that the town had been lucky each time began to exhaust even his supporters.

answerChoices.reasoning: Cheerfulness is a mood, but the sentence describes him making a claim about the facts, namely that three floods amounted to luck, which is a determined reading of misfortune as good fortune.
Stubbornness is captured already by 'insistence'; what wears on his supporters is the particular content of what he insists on, that repeated disaster counts as good fortune.
An evasive mayor would avoid characterizing the floods at all, while this one keeps offering a positive account of them.
Complacency is satisfaction that leads to inaction, but the sentence shows him actively and repeatedly asserting a favorable interpretation.
He is tiring his own supporters with reassurance, not attacking anyone.
His claim is perfectly clear, which is precisely why it grates after a third flood.
An apologetic mayor would accept blame, whereas this one is calling the town lucky.
Nothing in the sentence involves lawsuits or claims against anyone.
Calling three floods a run of luck is incompatible with gloom.
An alarmist would magnify the danger, the opposite of insisting the town got off lightly.
Relating to ships and sailing has no bearing on the mayor's attitude, flood or no flood.

sentenceSets.sentence: Critics dismissed the documentary as pollyannaish for ending on a single restored wetland while leaving the drained ten thousand acres offscreen.

answerChoices.reasoning: Sentimentality is an excess of feeling, but the objection here is structural: the film shows one recovery and withholds the vastly larger loss, producing a falsely hopeful picture.
'Selective' names the omission without saying which way it tilts, yet the critics' complaint is specifically that the choice leaves viewers with an unwarrantedly bright impression.
Superficiality is a failure to go deep, whereas this film's flaw is a slant, since it goes deep on the one wetland it chose to show.
Propaganda serves an identified sponsor's interest, but the sentence attributes the ending only to a rosy framing, with no beneficiary named.
The film's ending is described as pointedly focused on one site rather than as wandering.
Nothing suggests the documentary copied earlier work; the charge concerns what it left offscreen.
Permission to film is never at issue in the critics' objection.
The complaint is about the content of the ending, not about the film's length.
A harrowing film would confront viewers with the ten thousand drained acres instead of closing on a restoration.
Cynicism assumes the worst, the opposite of a closing image that suggests recovery is underway.
Existing below ground is a physical description and cannot characterize a documentary's outlook.
